# dodopayments_addon (Resource)

Manages a addon.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dodopayments_addon" "example" {
  currency     = "USD"
  name         = "example-addon"
  price        = 100
  tax_category = "digital_products"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `currency` (String) The currency of the Addon.
- `name` (String) Name of the Addon.
- `price` (Number) Amount of the addon.
- `tax_category` (String) Tax category applied to this Addon.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Optional description of the Addon. If you remove this attribute from the configuration, the API keeps the last value.
- `image_id` (String) Addon image id after its uploaded to S3.
Pass `null` to remove the existing image, omit to keep it unchanged.

### Read-Only

- `business_id` (String) Unique identifier for the business to which the addon belongs.
- `created_at` (String) Created time.
- `id` (String) id of the Addon.
- `image` (String) Image of the Addon.
- `updated_at` (String) Updated time.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = dodopayments_addon.example
  identity = {
    id = "<id>"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The ID of the addon.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = dodopayments_addon.example
  id = "<id>"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a addon by its ID.
terraform import dodopayments_addon.example <id>
```
